newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seek fuel to extend small gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares seek fuel to extend small gains.

text.p: German shares, bolstered by overnight Wall Street gains and a firmer dollar, were higher in early dealings on Tuesday as the DAX index sought fresh fuel to make a new advance on all-time record levels.
The IBIS DAX was up 42.12 points at 4,419.82 points and well above the DAX's closing level in bourse trade on Tuesday at 4,381.69 points.
"The fundamentals right now are actually very good to keep on posting gains but the buy orders are lacking at the moment," said one Frankfurt dealer.
The IBIS DAX has gained about 50 points so far this week from last Friday's closing level of 4,368 points but traders said profit-taking on any advance has capped gains.
"We keep trying to move higher but profit-taking keeps setting us back," said one dealer.
The market continued to focus on banks amid ongoing speculation for more mergers after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank announced last week their plans to merge.
BHF-Bank AG said it expected to post a satisfactory overall profit for 1997 after group pre-tax profit rose 10.4 percent to 181 million marks in the first six months.
Shares in BHF, considered a top takeover target, were stable in IBIS trade at 59 marks as dealers said the results were generally in line with market expectations.
But other banking shares posted gains as Deutsche Bank AG rose 2.95 marks to 123.15 marks, Commerzbank AG rose 1.01 marks to 62 marks and Dresdner Bank AG rose 1.68 marks to 85.50 marks.
Hypo-Bank was up 1.85 marks at 78.10 marks, while Vereinsbank advanced 3.30 marks to 102.70 marks.
"The whole sector is up on speculation for more deals," said one trader. "It's a key factor driving the DAX higher."
Carmaker BMW AG was among the top gainers, rising 42.50 marks to 1,455 marks after falling on Tuesday on first half results that dealers said were above expectations.
Volkswagen AG was also higher, rising 16 marks to 1,367 marks after saying in recent days that it was adding extra shifts at some VW and Audi factories due to high demand.

Among shares trading against the DAX trend and posting losses were electronics group Siemens AG, which was down 85 pfennigs at 128.60 marks, and retailer Karstadt AG, which was down 90 pfennigs at 719 marks.
